title: Submarine Groundwater Discharge (SGD) calculation in R
text: Submarine fresh groundwater discharge (SFGD) critical pathway nutrient transport marine ecosystems, yet quantification often hindered sparse infrequent data coastal zones. SGDr presents parsimonious methodology estimating SFGD data-sparse settings integrating simple modelling techniques characterize coastal aquifer water fluxes. combines soil water balance model lumped-parameter representation aquifer, incorporating freshwater-seawater interface. simplicity enables rapid calibration uncertainty analysis, supporting land-use decisions field investigations.

title: Submarine Groundwater Discharge (SGD) calculation in R
text: calculate SFGD using estimate_sgd(), input data required includes: Daily precipitation (R [mm]) Evapotranspiration (E0 [mm]) Pumping rate (q1 [m3/d]) Initial groundwater table (hf [mm]) Initial water table two soil buckets. (phi1, phi2 [mm]) example input file: parameters stored using JSON format (.json). Two types parameter JSON files required: Calibratable Parameters JSON File: Contains parameters adjustable subject calibration model optimization. Constant Parameters JSON File: Contains fixed parameters remain unchanged throughout model run. Use json_to_parameter_list convert JSON files list: SFGD can calculated : estimated results can visualized plot:    GUI made shiny also available:
code: library(SGDr) test_data <- read.csv(SGDr_example('test_data.csv')) head(test_data) #>   t R  E0 phi1 phi2  hf       q1 #> 1 1 0 4.2   25  100 1.5 205.3388 #> 2 2 0 4.7    0    0 0.0 205.3388 #> 3 3 0 5.2    0    0 0.0 205.3388 #> 4 4 0 6.0    0    0 0.0 205.3388 #> 5 5 0 7.9    0    0 0.0 205.3388 #> 6 6 0 5.0    0    0 0.0 205.3388 cali_pars <- json_to_parameter_list(SGDr_example('preferred.json')) cnst_pars <- json_to_parameter_list(SGDr_example('consts.json')) results <- estimate_sgd(test_data, cali_pars, cnst_pars, 120, 1500) results #>  #> SGD Estimation Summary #> Warning in summary.SGD_ESTIMATION_DF(x, ...): No base date available. Please provide the base date to calculate the simulation period. #> Simulation length:  19884 days #> Estimated SFGD (q0):  1.16 m2/d #> Estimated Recharge (Wnet):  0.19 mm/d #> Estimated Runoff (Q):  0.38 mm/d #> Median hn: 1.73 m #> Median xn: 8539.46 m # use summary summary(results, base_date = '19670101') #>  #> SGD Estimation Summary #> Simlation period: 1967-01-01 - 2021-06-09  #> Estimated SFGD (q0):  1.16 m2/d #> Estimated Recharge (Wnet):  0.19 mm/d #> Estimated Runoff (Q):  0.38 mm/d #> Median hn: 1.73 m #> Median xn: 8539.46 m # use print  print(results, base_date = '19670101') #>  #> SGD Estimation Summary #> Simlation period: 1967-01-01 - 2021-06-09  #> Estimated SFGD (q0):  1.16 m2/d #> Estimated Recharge (Wnet):  0.19 mm/d #> Estimated Runoff (Q):  0.38 mm/d #> Median hn: 1.73 m #> Median xn: 8539.46 m # visualize the prediction results plot(results, base_date = '19670101') # visualize the input data plot(results, base_date = '19670101', type = 'input') # compare with the observed groundwater table library(data.table) obs_data <- data.table::fread(SGDr_example('obs_data.csv')) plot(results, y = obs_data, base_date = '19670101', type = 'comp')

title: Estimate the SFGD (q0 [m2/d]) . — estimate_sgd
text: Estimate SGD volume based Strack (1976) analytical solution. inputData data.frame containing required columns model (R, E0, q1, hf, phi1, phi2). R numeric vector daily precipitation (mm). E0 numeric vector daily potential evapotranspiration (mm). q1 numeric vector daily pumping rate (m3/d). hf numeric vector initial groundwater level (mm), first value used initial value SB1. phi1 numeric vector initial water level first soil bucket (mm). first value used initial value SB1. phi2 numeric vector inital water level second soil bucket (mm). first value used initial value SB2. calibratableParams list calibratable parameters. recommended use json_to_paramter_list create list. nw integer indicating period want average recharge. warmup integer indicating number days warm model.
